item.title: India dominate Zimbabwe in Vadodara as Harmanpreet, Deepti and Vaishnavi headline 121-run win
item.description: India Women produced a commanding all-round performance to seal the three-match ODI series against Zimbabwe with a game to spare, registering a 121-run victory in the second ODI at the BCA Stadium in Vadodara on Sunday. Twin centuries from Harmanpreet Kaur and Deepti Sharma powered the hosts to a mammoth 328/6 before the bowlers dismantled Zimbabwe for 207 in 48.5 overs to secure an unassailable 2-0 lead. Harmanpreet, Deepti power India to imposing total India suffered an early setback when skipper Smriti Mandhana fell for a duck, but Pratika Rawal steadied the innings with a composed 61 off 67 balls. She shared a 124-run partnership for the third wicket with Harmanpreet, laying the foundation for a big total. Harmanpreet took charge with a fluent 126 off 121 deliveries, striking 15 boundaries, while Deepti provided the late impetus with an unbeaten 106 off 86 balls. Deepti reached her century in just 83 deliveries, producing an aggressive counter-attacking knock that kept Zimbabwe's bowlers under pressure. The pair added 153 runs off 138 balls for the fifth wicket, setting a new record for India's highest partnership for that wicket in women's ODIs. Their efforts lifted the hosts to 328/6 in 50 overs, leaving Zimbabwe with a daunting target of 329. Nomvelo Sibanda was Zimbabwe's most successful bowler, claiming two wickets, but the visitors struggled to contain India's batters through the middle overs. Vaishnavi, Deepti lead India's bowling charge Zimbabwe showed greater resistance in the chase than they had in the opening match, with Modester Mupachikwa and Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano putting together a 69-run partnership to give the visitors some hope. Mupachikwa made 49 off 70 balls, while Mugeri-Tiripano scored 46, but both fell in the 40s as India broke the partnership at a crucial stage. Zimbabwe were forced to rebuild, and the wickets continued to tumble as the required run rate climbed. Vaishnavi, who returned to the XI in place of Kranti Gaud, made a decisive impact in the middle and lower overs, finishing with figures of 4/39 in 10 overs. Her disciplined bowling prevented Zimbabwe from building further partnerships and gave India control of the contest. Deepti capped a memorable outing with the ball as well, taking 3/32 in nine overs after her century earlier in the day. Jintimani Kalita then claimed the final wicket of Chiedza Dhururu for her maiden international wicket, bowling Zimbabwe out for 207 in 48.5 overs.

item.title: Real Madrid star forced off with injury vs Barcelona
item.description: Real Madrid star forced off with injury vs Barcelona La Liga giants Real Madrid have on Sunday evening been dealt a concerning setback on the personnel front. This comes after Federico Valverde was forced out of the club’s showdown with Barcelona. Los Blancos are of course currently locked in action at the Spotify Camp Nou, in the new season’s first edition of El Clásico. The aforementioned Valverde featured from the off in the matchup, again favoured to both Trent Alexander-Arnold and Denzel Dumfries at right-back for the visitors. During the first-half, however, the Uruguayan appeared to pick up a fitness problem, after making a challenge in the middle of the park. Valverde from here carried on, but all the while appeared to be moving gingerly. It therefore came as little surprise when Real Madrid’s captain ultimately succumbed to his complaint just beyond the hour mark. Valverde was replaced by Denzel Dumfries, ahead of undergoing a round of medical scans back in Spain’s capital over the days ahead. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: F1 standings after United States GP as Kimi Antonelli closes in on 2026 title
item.description: Formula 1 returns to the Circuit of the Americas this weekend for the United States Grand Prix - as Kimi Antonelli stands on the cusp of his first world championship. The 20-year-old Italian holds a 102-point lead over Mercedes teammate George Russell and will win his first title if he wins this Sunday’s grand prix and Russell finishes ninth or lower. Antonelli, who starts on pole, also needs Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton to finish fifth or lower. A podium last time out in Singapore extended Antonelli’s lead, as Max Verstappen claimed his second victory in a row amid a Red Bull resurgence this season. Russell, meanwhile, only finished ninth and crashed out of the sprint race in Marina Bay. The popular race in Austin is the start of another triple-header, with Mexico and Brazil to follow in the weeks ahead. Verstappen was victorious at COTA last year. item.title: 'Let's talk over here.' Trey Hendrickson has private chat with Burrow
item.description: Baltimore Ravens edge rusher Trey Hendrickson, who played five seasons for the Cincinnati Bengals , met with Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow on the field after Hendrickson's NFL Week 7 loss to his former team at M&T Bank Stadium. Burrow started to talk to Hendrickson as the two were surrounded by reporters and photographers. "Let's talk over here," Hendrickson said, as the two left the media scrum for a more private conversation. "See you guys!" During the first half, Hendrickson reached Burrow as Burrow looked to pass, but Burrow got rid of the ball just before Hendrickson would've sacked him. Hendrickson helped Burrow up after taking him to the ground. During the week, Hendrickson was asked what he would say to those who suggest there was bad blood when he left Cincinnati. "As a Christian, I forgive and obviously I move on," Hendrickson said . "And there's some wonderful times that I had there. Like I said, there'll be a time to reflect and all that stuff. But right now, there's an opponent in front of us. And as the Ravens, we look forward to capitalizing on everything that we can this week." Earlier in the week, Ravens linebacker Trenton Simpson predicted a multi-sack game for Hendrickson against his former team. Hendrickson, who led the NFL in sacks in 2024 , entered Week 7 with two sacks in the four games in which he's played for the Ravens this season. He missed two games because of finger surgery. item.title: Steelers trade flash for force, find 3rd-down success vs. Saints
item.description: (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers’ offense wasn’t a fireworks show against the New Orleans Saints, it was a cement truck. Pittsburgh out rushed New Orleans 148-18 and averaged just under five yards per carry. This efficiency in the run game allowed the Steelers to establish long drives of eight, 13, 11, 14, and 11 plays. The Steelers had just one three-and-out on the day, which was a welcome change from the five they had against the Buccaneers. A big part of establishing those long drives was their efficiency on third down. Pittsburgh entered the week as the NFL’s worst team on third down in terms of EPA per play, and they were 28th in conversion percentage. On Sunday, Pittsburgh converted a season-high 10 third downs on 16 attempts. Their biggest play of the game came on 3rd-and-14 when Aaron Rodgers extended the play and found DK Metcalf for a 51-yard completion, which set up the Darnell Washington touchdown. The run game working so well helped the Steelers stay within a respectable distance on those third downs, as their average play on third down was under six yards, per Sumer Sports . With the majority of those plays being 3rd-and-short or 3rd-and-medium, this allowed Pittsburgh to run on a good chunk of their third down plays. Ahead of Week 7, the Steelers didn’t run the ball on third down more than three times – they did so seven times on Sunday and converted six of them into first downs, which doubled their previous season-high of three rushes for first downs on third down. There were points left on the board, and Aaron Rodgers said as much after the game. They were unable to finish two drives in which they made it to the red zone and had to settle for field goals, and another drive reached the Saints’ 29 yard-line that also ended with a field goal. However, it’s much better to see that while still being 5-2 and in first place in the division than it would be had they found a way to lose to New Orleans. The scoreboard may not have been pretty, but the way they got there was beautiful – running the ball well, succeeding on third down, and sustaining long drives. Those are the characteristics of an efficient offense, and you can beat just about anybody if you can do that on a consistent basis. Let us know what you think in the comments . item.title: Chargers take charge of 2027 NFL Draft tank race with Dolphins’ upset of Jets
item.description: William Purnell-Imagn Images Chargers take charge of 2027 NFL Draft tank race with Dolphins’ upset of Jets appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . A new leader emerged in the race to land the top pick of the 2027 NFL Draft Sunday. The Miami Dolphins just placed the Los Angeles Chargers at the top there. All thanks to Miami stunning the New York Jets . The Dolphins left LAC as the last winless team left in claiming the 28-25 victory. And that win becomes the first for head coach Jeff Hafley. But out in Los Angeles, Miami’s win doesn’t bode well for the Chargers. Unless there are fans who hope to see the Bolts land the top overall pick. There’s a growing population of fans who believe the string has run out for quarterback Justin Herbert . The past first round selection and Pro Bowler hasn’t won a playoff game in his career. Furthermore, he’s thrown more interceptions (eight) than touchdowns (five). Still, his head coach Jim Harbaugh insist he’s got lots of confidence in his passer despite the stunning 0-6 start. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) But the Chargers would walk into a growingly intriguing QB class for the April draft. Texas quarterback Arch Manning helped reignite his stock by beating top 10 opponent Ole Miss on Saturday. The Rebels’ Trinidad Chambliss also is garnering praise and comes with a College Football Playoff background. Yet Drew Mestemaker from Oklahoma State is shooting up the boards, who has the Cowboys at 5-2 overall. Mestemaker has tossed 20 touchdowns to only six interceptions. Plus he’s thriving in the same Air Raid system that produced Kansas City Chiefs three-time Super Bowl winner Patrick Mahomes. So the Bolts now sit with the top pick in the draft. Of course, it could change throughout the course of the year. There had been hope Ratcliffe, a boyhood United fan, would change that when he struck a deal with the Glazers to become a minority shareholder on Christmas Eve 2023. Instead, a succession of decisions have led to major questions over his handling of the club. On the management side, United's hierarchy eventually backed Erik ten Hag after talking with alternatives in the wake of the shock 2024 FA Cup final triumph over Manchester City, spending over £200m on the likes of Leny Yoro, Matthijs de Ligt and Manuel Ugarte. Last week, Ten Hag told the Athletic the club went back on a promise not to sell homegrown Scotland international Scott McTominay to fund Ugarte's £50m move from Paris St-Germain. The 'Standards' banner that was held up on the Stretford End showing the images of legendary skippers Bryan Robson, Eric Cantona and Roy Keane was there to remind the executives running the club of the history they should be aspiring to. If that wasn't enough, a ticket touting investigation launched in the summer led to condemnation from all United's major fan groups. The club argued they were trying to catch touts, while fans felt it was an attempt to drive regular match-goers out in favour of more corporate sales. The club are adamant that is not the case, but the argument is falling on deaf ears. The same is also true of plans for a new 100,000-capacity stadium. item.title: Cam Skattebo confirms injury after Giants beat Texans in overtime
item.description: As he was running the New York Giants to a victory over the Houston Texans in overtime on Sunday, running back Cam Skattebo pulled up with an apparent injury. After the Giants forced a Texans punt on the opening drive of overtime, Skattebo ripped off a 42-yard run but slid down during the play right before he was about to get tackled. As we figured, Skattebo did indeed suffer an injury, which he confirmed after the game. The second-year back told ESPN’s Dan Graziano that he has a hamstring injury. “Cam Skattebo said he wasn’t sliding on purpose on the play that set up Devin Singletary’s game-winning touchdown,” Graziano relayed . “Said he felt something in his hamstring and knew they were in FG range so he slid.” MORE: NFL Week 7 TV schedule – full list of games and start times Thankfully, as Skattebo pointed out, the Giants have a bye week, so he’ll have a few weeks to get himself right before New York returns to action in Week 9 against the Washington Commanders. “Good thing we have a bye week,” Skattebo said. item.title: Jesse Minter says Ravens are 'too much of a momentum team'
item.description: Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter talked about what went wrong after halftime in his team's 35-13 Week 7 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals at M&T Bank Stadium. "Tale of two halves obviously," Minter told reporters after the game. "Team came out ready to roll. I didn't feel like we took advantage of enough opportunities in the first half to continue to create separation. And then you know in the second half, they made a few plays early (and) got momentum." "Once we lost momentum, you know, right now we're too much of a momentum team," Minter continued. "So we're riding the wave when it's good, and we're riding the wave when it's bad. I think that's a main focus for us to be able to stay a little bit more even keel and continue to make plays and do things. And so credit to them for the second half." The Bengals became just the 10th team in NFL history to get shut out in the first half and then score 35 points or more in the second half, per CBS Sports research. item.title: Ravens’ latest blown double-digit lead is most spectacular collapse yet
item.description: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images Ravens’ latest blown double-digit lead is most spectacular collapse yet appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . On Sunday, the Baltimore Ravens took their second straight loss with a home defeat at the hands of the Cincinnati Bengals. The Ravens played this one once again without quarterback Lamar Jackson , who was injured, with Tyler Huntley getting the start instead. The Ravens took a 13-0 lead into the halftime locker room in this one, but ultimately ended up getting outscored 35-0 in the second half for an ugly 35-13 loss. Baltimore has a history of blowing double-digit leads, dating back to the days of John Harbaugh, but it’s rare that such a lead ends up turning into a true blowout loss, making Sunday’s defeat against the divisional rival Bengals all the more troubling. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Meanwhile, the Ravens will certainly hope for good news on the Jackson front, as the star has now missed three straight games due to an ankle injury he suffered against the Tennessee Titans a few weeks ago. While Tyler Huntley played well in his first start against the Atlanta Falcons, he has since fallen back down to Earth, and the Ravens now sit in last place in the AFC North, thanks to the Pittsburgh Steelers’ win over the New Orleans Saints earlier in the day. How many of the Ravens’ troubles can be attributed to Jackson’s injury alone and how many are more systemic in nature is certainly a fair question to ask at this point, but head coach Jesse Minter and his staff certainly have their work cut out for them heading into next week against the Buffalo Bills. item.title: What Bill Self said on the health of Kohl Rosario, Trey Kaufman-Renn
item.description: LAWRENCE — Prior to tip-off Sunday, ahead of an exhibition against Duke, Kansas basketball coach Bill Self shared a couple of health updates on his roster. Self, speaking in a game preview video KU posted to its social media account on X, highlighted that sophomore guard Kohl Rosario wouldn’t play after suffering a concussion recently in practice. According to Self, Rosario caught an elbow in the mouth. Rosario needed 14 stitches and some form of oral surgery. Self also mentioned that fifth-year forward Trey Kaufman-Renn wouldn’t play either. Self explained that, while he wasn’t going to put Kaufman-Renn in just to get him in shape, Kaufman-Renn was also nicked up in a recent practice. Kaufman-Renn was able to practice Saturday, however. Fast forward to postgame, after a 90-84 loss against Duke, and Self provided a little more information on how Rosario and Kaufman-Renn were doing. While Kansas is relatively healthy overall, both have the potential to contribute when fully available. There’s also a lot of anticipation surrounding what Kaufman-Renn could mean for the team this season. RELATED: Kansas basketball vs Duke exhibition final score, analysis “Trey did turn his ankle the other day, but he’ll be fine,” Self told reporters after the exhibition. “Hopefully, he’s 100% and be ready to go. His conditioning isn’t great. We’ve seen how good he is, but I’d say from a conditioning standpoint he’s — I didn’t want to really put him out there, I think, if he’s not ready and pulls a groin or something. Then that sets us back too far.” Self continued: “Kohl, probably, will be out until at least mid-week.” Kansas has some time to get both of them ready, ahead of the start of the regular season Nov. 2 at home against Fordham. There’s also another mid-major game after that, Nov. 6 at home against Middle Tennessee, before the schedule becomes much more difficult. There’s the Champions Classic matchup against No. 23 Kentucky on Nov. 10 in Chicago, and the Players Era event in Las Vegas as the month of November unfolds. KU, ranked tied for No. 18 in the preseason coaches poll, has aspirations of being a contender both in the Big 12 Conference and nationally. While the Jayhawks lost their two major exhibitions at home this preseason, against No. 2 Duke and No. 11 Louisville, both defeats were close and showed Kansas can compete with some of the nation’s best. It’s just a matter of KU learning from those matchups and developing over the course of the season. Jordan Guskey covers University of Kansas Athletics at The Topeka Capital-Journal. Late in the game, with the 49ers down six and facing a 3rd & 4 at the Atlanta 47, Brandin Cooks had a false start, backing the Niners up, and Brock Purdy had an interception on the next play. Then, perhaps one of the costliest miscues of the day was Eddy Piniero’s missed extra point on the 49ers final touchdown. Hitting that would’ve had the Niners down eight on their final possession, but the miss kept it a two-score game and highly unlikely for a comeback. Maybe it doesn’t matter anyways with George Kittle’s fumble, but that problem has been a recurring one for the 49ers special teams unit this year. San Francisco had seven penalties in this game, and a lot of them were in costly situations. Turnovers You’re very rarely going to win a game when you have four turnovers and the opposing team has zero. Well, the 49ers had a ton of chances to win this one, even in the final minutes, but their turnovers were all brutal, which was too much to overcome on top of the self-inflicted wounds. Up 14-9 in the second quarter and driving in Arizona territory, the 49ers got lucky when a Jordan James fumble was recovered by Luke Farrell, setting San Francisco up with a 2nd & 1 at the Atlanta 28. Well, it didn’t matter as Kaelon Black coughed the ball up on the next play. San Francisco was in scoring range and ended with no points. To make matters worse, Atlanta ate up the final 4:20 of clock, kicking a field goal to end the half and starting the second half with the ball, where they scored a touchdown. Major turnaround there. The 49ers’ second turnover also came with the Niners driving well into Atlanta territory. On 2nd & 14 from the Atlanta 25, Brock Purdy escaped the pocket, rolling to his right, and seemed to be trying to hit Jacob Cowing. But Cowing didn’t roll with his quarterback, and Purdy’s pass was intercepted by a diving Jesse Bates, who made a great play. Should Purdy have thrown this one away. Probably. Did Cowing also make a mistake? Looked like it. That’s another scoring opportunity wiped off the board, and Atlanta responded well, going 11 plays and 90 yards for a touchdown to extend their lead to 26-14. That five-possession swing was the ballgame. On top of the four turnovers, the 49ers also had the turnover on downs, which, once again, came on a drive where San Francisco was deep in Atlanta territory. Interestingly enough, the models said to kick on 4th & 10 at the Atlanta 23, but with the 49ers down 12 and the defense struggling to get a stop, Kyle Shanahan went for it and Brock Purdy was sacked. In hindsight, the 49ers have a shot if they kicked there, but the process also made sense from a go-for perspective. Then, San Francisco had a big chance to take the lead down six after the defense forced back-to-back three-and-outs. With just over four minutes left, the 49ers got the ball at their own 47-yard line. They got to a 3rd & 4, but Brandin Cooks’s false start pushed them back five, and the defense made a great play on Brock Purdy’s second interception, which essentially sealed the deal. It was a rough game for the 49ers, to say the least. Niners defense contains damage The 49ers defense had some back-breaking penalties in this one. But it was encouraging that they held Bijan Robinson to 63 yards on 20 carries, while also having a good game in the red zone. The 49ers forced three field goals in the red zone in this one, mitigating some of the defense, while they gave up only 4.7 yards per play. There were some long drives where the penalties hurt, and the 49ers could not get off the field. That needs to be cleaned up, as Atlanta had drives of 10, 14, 10, and 11 plays, resulting in 23 of their points. But on a day when the offense had four turnovers, there were some solid things to take away from Raheem Morris’s unit, as the coordinator tried to create a plan to disrupt the quick game of Michael Penix. Now, the secondary has been leaky two weeks in a row. There have been far too many penalties from that group, including a few that were killer in extending Atlanta drives. item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. item.title: Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent off
item.description: There are days when Tottenham go into these big games and find ways to beat themselves. This time, though, they held their nerve at a ground where they have mostly only known doom. Spurs played with control, stayed patient and won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018 after waiting for Chelsea to press the self-destruct button during a calamitous and comical ending to a cagey game. Chelsea were meant to have grown. Xabi Alonso had even praised his side’s emotional control and ability to manage awkward spells during the buildup, but perhaps that was asking for trouble. Chelsea, short of poise on and off the pitch, deserved to be beaten at home for the first time this season and there was plenty of blame to go around after Alonso got his tactics wrong, Mike Penders scored a ridiculous own goal and Cole Palmer was sent off after a lunge on Conor Gallagher when he was already on a booking. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. Nothing erudite, anyway. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
